Not sure why the article wants to bash Nielson about not getting with the times, but it feels like the author doesn't understand what Nielson is. They exist as a neutral 3rd party to assess what advertising on any give program. Since Netflix doesn't sell advertising, why would they need someone to verify their viewship for advertisers? As much as the author would like to have Nielson numbers for Netflix viewer data, nobody has any reason to pay for that research.

Hoping for netflix to get with the times might be a valid argument for youtube or hulu, since they are both advertiser-funded. But since both services can generate the data that advertisers want on the server-side, I'm not sure that Nielson will have much of a roll after the end of the broadcast era.
